conclusions: Both independent live runs expose Rocks then tentacles-to-Lava over phases one and two; each phase-two warning set exactly matches the three turn-entry Mech positions.
Both phase-two warning sets become persistent terrain-id-3 tiles on the following board; the historical bridge serialized final-island Lava as water.

Run 20260430_230740_117 exposes the source-constrained six-tile phase-three cluster, converts all six to Road/Ground including two prior Lava tiles, and exposes a complete cardinal phase-four crossing row.
Run 20260506_114649_974 proves a phase-one falling rock converts a Mountain to Road/Ground, while its non-atomic phase-three and phase-four samples remain explicit timing ambiguities.
limitations: The historical recording schema does not attest executable, depot, scripts-revision, map-revision, environment object identity, or scheduler callback identity, so these runs corroborate but do not build-key the current Windows source inventory.

The old bridge scanned Board:IsEnvironmentDanger separately from the environment object. Its warning order is not proof of native Locations order, and Instant phases can be sampled at ambiguous boundaries.
The recordings do not prove BigBomb exclusion, future RNG call order, Env_Final:Start's unused LavaPath, exact native Plan/ApplyEffect callback timing, or enemy Board:SetDangerous behavior.

No historical selected tile contains a live Massive, flying, Shielded, or Frozen pawn at resolution. Those lethal rules remain exact-source/general-DAMAGE_DEATH contracts covered by focused simulator tests.
Phase-four aftermath and the surface-to-cave or mission-end handoff are not captured by a later same-stage atomic checkpoint.
